text: Later that morning. <break time="0.8s" /> I climbed to the top of the mountain. <break time="0.8s" /> To look for a search party. <break time="0.8s" /> But all I saw. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a quiet valley. <break time="0.8s" /> And one farmer. <break time="0.8s" /> Plowing a field with a mule. <break time="0.8s" /> Perhaps they have not noticed yet. <break time="0.8s" /> That the boy is missing. <break time="0.8s" /> I said to myself. <break time="0.8s" /> When I returned to the cave. <break time="0.8s" /> I found Bill backed against the wall. <break time="0.8s" /> Breathing hard. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy had put. <break time="0.8s" /> A hot boiled potato. <break time="0.8s" /> Down his back. <break time="0.8s" /> And now he was holding a big rock. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the boy took a sling. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of his pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> And shot a stone at Bill. <break time="0.8s" /> It hit him. <break time="0.8s" /> Behind the left ear. <break time="0.8s" /> So hard that he fell over beside the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> You will not go away. <break time="0.8s" /> And leave me here alone. <break time="0.8s" /> Will you, Sam. <break time="0.8s" /> Bill asked weakly. <break time="0.8s" /> I told the boy that I would take him straight home. <break time="0.8s" /> If he did not behave. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy quickly promised. <break time="0.8s" /> To be good. <break time="0.8s" /> As long as he could play the Black Scout. <break time="0.8s" /> That day. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Bill and I sat down. <break time="0.8s" /> To write a letter to old Dorset. <break time="0.8s" /> Asking for a ransom.
